api.a2a.exempt: The A2A entry is for other agents (third-party clients or another Daisy), not a command of the owner's; on the owner's side use daisy request / grant / agent
api.error.runnerJsonBroken: {why}: fix runner.json (or move it away) before setting the update source
api.error.runnerJsonUntrusted: {file} {why}: check what it says and make it this account's and owner-only (chmod go-w) before setting the update source
api.error.serverFault: Internal server error; see the server log
api.exempt.autostart: Provided by the local command daisy autostart (it must work while Daisy is not running, so it is a local command; it shares this route's logic)
api.exempt.platformOnly: For the external platform that mirrors notification settings (the backend of a UI embedding Daisy), not an action of the owner's; the owner changes settings with daisy notify set
api.exempt.update: Provided by the local command daisy update (--check / --apply / --rollback / --source): while Daisy is not running it does the same steps itself; while it runs it calls this route
api.field.access.allow: Open the terminal, command execution and directory browsing on the outside face (all off by default)
api.field.access.host: Listen address: overlay network address, 0.0.0.0, loopback address (for other programs on the same machine to visit), etc.; do not write localhost
api.field.access.origins: Allowed external UI origins, each written as `https://host[:port]` (no path, no trailing slash, no wildcards); `http://` is allowed only for local loopback (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1], for development). Empty list = none allowed
api.field.access.port: Port; if empty, derived from the uid (from 29600)
api.field.access.tls: TLS by default (self-signed certificate); false (plain HTTP) is allowed only on loopback, overlay network or private network addresses
api.field.ai-token.audience: The party to access (the token's aud). Cannot be this Daisy itself: access it with the current turn's AI work credential
api.field.ai-token.scope: Scopes wanted, space-separated; cannot exceed what the owner has, and never includes daisy:grant
api.field.audit.action: Only this action's (e.g. api.session.create, access.denied, pin.grant)
api.field.audit.after: Only those after this sequence number (continue from the last read)
api.field.audit.before: Paging: the next from the previous page's answer
api.field.audit.channel: Only this channel's: web, device, cli, issuer, a2a, ai, system, none
api.field.audit.limit: Maximum number of records (1–500, default 100), newest to oldest
api.field.audit.limit2: Maximum number of lines (default 200), newest last
api.field.audit.outcome: Only this outcome's: ok, denied, error
api.field.audit.route: Only this endpoint's (e.g. session.cancel) or tool's (e.g. tool.wakeup)
api.field.audit.session: Only this session's AI (or what was done for its turn)
api.field.audit.since: Only those at or after this time (milliseconds)
api.field.contacts.cardFile: Card file (.daisycard, same content as the text); use either this or card
api.field.contacts.cardText: The card's text: the whole block the other person exported (a few human-readable lines plus a final line daisy-card:1:…), or just that last line; line breaks and spaces inserted in the middle are removed
api.field.contacts.direct: Direct addresses (this Daisy's outside face root address); can be several. If neither this nor relay is given, the address the outside face is listening on is used (no address if it is off)
api.field.contacts.expectId: The identity number you checked with the other person (the first 16 or more characters are enough): the card is refused if its identity number does not match
api.field.contacts.id: The contact's identity number (spaces allowed, case-insensitive), or its first 8 or more characters (as long as no one else shares them), or its URN
api.field.contacts.name: Display name on the card; if omitted, the owner's account name on this machine
api.field.contacts.note: A one-line note, e.g. "the server at work"
api.field.contacts.relay: Fixed addresses given by the relay; can be several
api.field.contacts.update: When this person is already in contacts, replace the old card with this (newer) one; if omitted, answers 409 and lists the differences
api.field.contacts.whitelist: Also add them to the allowlist: when they call your agents that are "open to everyone mutually recognised", no card pops up. When updating an existing contact, leaving it out keeps it as it is
api.field.devices.code: Pairing code (XXXXX-XXXXX; case, spaces and dashes don't matter)
api.field.devices.deviceName: The device's name (at most {deviceNameMax} characters), e.g. "My phone"
api.field.devices.name: A name for this device; if empty, the name the device reports itself (the browser name) is used
api.field.devices.name2: The name this device reports for itself (not used when the owner named it on the pairing code)
api.field.devices.secret: The device credential obtained when pairing (ddev_…)
api.field.events.after: Answer only events whose seq is greater than this (the cursor from the last answer), default 0
api.field.events.wait: Long poll: with no new events, wait at most this many seconds (0–{eventsWaitMaxS}); a new event is answered at once
api.field.invoke.act: Whether act is allowed: true lets others, with an "act" mark, ask this AI to work on the main line (queued after your current turn); false turns it off, so calls with the mark are all rejected (ACT_DISABLED), while ask stays available
api.field.invoke.decision: Always allow (always: records a grant, so this person is not asked again when calling this agent; all waiting calls are let through), allow once (once: lets through only the call that raised this card; other calls waiting at the same time move to a new card and are asked again), reject (reject: all waiting calls are rejected, and calls again within 10 minutes are rejected outright)
api.field.invoke.listed: Named people: contacts' identity numbers (or a unique prefix of 8 or more characters). With listed, this is the list; if omitted, the existing list is kept
api.field.invoke.note: A note (recorded only on the card)
api.field.invoke.openTo: all: open to everyone mutually recognised (the first call pops up a card; people on the allowlist pass directly); listed: open only to named people (those on the list pass directly; everyone else is rejected, with no card)
api.field.invoke.permissionMode: Which permission mode act uses: one of this AI's permission modes (the modes from GET), or session = follow the session's own (the profile's). Cannot be a mode that skips all confirmations
api.field.invoke.public: true: make it public (people you mutually recognise can call it over A2A according to the audience; conversations mix, see the description); false: make it private again (calls in progress stop; grants, audience and ask/act settings are cleared)
api.field.issuer.audience: This Daisy's audience identifier at the issuer, used to verify the token's aud; if empty, this Daisy's URN
api.field.issuer.clientId: The client id used when proving itself to the token endpoint (private_key_jwt); if empty, this Daisy's URN plus #client
api.field.issuer.issuer: The issuer identifier; must equal the iss of the tokens it signs: an https address (http only on this machine's loopback 127.0.0.1 / [::1], with DAISY_ALLOW_HTTP_ISSUER=1 set and no other people's accounts on this machine — for tests and local deployments)
api.field.issuer.jwksUri: Public key set (JWKS) address; taken from the metadata when left out: an https address (http only on this machine's loopback 127.0.0.1 / [::1], with DAISY_ALLOW_HTTP_ISSUER=1 set and no other people's accounts on this machine — for tests and local deployments)
api.field.issuer.metadataUrl: Metadata address (RFC 8414 / OpenID Connect Discovery); derived from the issuer identifier when left out: an https address (http only on this machine's loopback 127.0.0.1 / [::1], with DAISY_ALLOW_HTTP_ISSUER=1 set and no other people's accounts on this machine — for tests and local deployments)
api.field.issuer.ownerSubject: Which subject (sub) is this Daisy's owner: only its tokens get the owner's identity
api.field.issuer.ownerToken: The owner's token (signed by the issuer for the owner, without act, lifetime exp - iat at most 24 hours): used only to exchange tokens for the AI (subject_token), not to log in to this Daisy; stored in a file only the owner can read
api.field.issuer.tokenEndpoint: Token endpoint (RFC 8693 token exchange); taken from the metadata when left out: an https address (http only on this machine's loopback 127.0.0.1 / [::1], with DAISY_ALLOW_HTTP_ISSUER=1 set and no other people's accounts on this machine — for tests and local deployments)
api.field.notifications.after: Cursor: answer only items that changed after it (the cursor from the last answer)
api.field.notifications.device: Use this device's notification settings to work out whether each one alerts (alert)
api.field.operations.ids: Ids of the selected queued messages
api.field.pin.grant: PIN grant: put it in the daisy-pin-grant request header
api.field.pin.lockedUntil: When locked after consecutive wrong tries, until when (millisecond timestamp); null when not locked
api.field.pin.newPin: The new PIN ({pinMinLength}–{pinMaxLength} characters; digits only is fine)
api.field.pin.oldPin: The old PIN: required when one is already set
api.field.pin.resetAt: When the PIN was most recently reset locally (millisecond timestamp)
api.field.pin.resetVia: The entry point of the most recent reset
api.field.pin.set: Whether a PIN has been set (no AI turns start until it is)
api.field.pin.setAt: When the PIN was most recently set or changed (millisecond timestamp)
api.field.pin.setVia: The entry point of the most recent set or change
api.field.prompts.note2: This session's supplementary note; null clears it
api.field.prompts.sections: Toggles for optional sections; null means back to the default
api.field.prompts.sections2: Toggles for optional sections; null means follow your personal settings
api.field.relay.acme: Request a certificate for the relay address from a certificate authority (ACME TLS-ALPN-01, Let's Encrypt by default). If off, only a self-signed certificate is used: then only Daisy-to-Daisy traffic works through the relay
api.field.relay.acmeDirectory: ACME directory URL (https), Let's Encrypt by default; can be another certificate authority that supports TLS-ALPN-01
api.field.relay.address: The relay's own address, e.g. relay.example or https://relay.example:8443 (domain and port only)
api.field.residents.approvals: Operations that still need a person's confirmation in auto mode: reject = refuse automatically (default; the task continues or fails without waiting); owner = send to the owner to confirm (the task stays working)
api.field.residents.concurrency: Maximum visiting conversations at once (default 4); tasks beyond that wait queued as "submitted" and are not dropped
api.field.residents.dailyTurns: Maximum turns per 24 hours (0 = unlimited, at most 1000); calls past the limit are refused with QUOTA_EXCEEDED
api.field.residents.description: One sentence on what service it offers (the card's description)
api.field.residents.dirs: Directories it may use besides the workspace (absolute paths, repeatable); only harnesses that declare support can set this (Claude Code)
api.field.residents.harness: Which harness to use (claude, codex, kimi, opencode, ...)
api.field.residents.instructions: Prompt layer three, "instructions": how to answer, what it may and may not do
api.field.residents.knowledge: Prompt layer four, "knowledge": background material it can cite
api.field.residents.name: Name: the title on the agent's card
api.field.residents.permissionMode: Permission mode: one of this harness's permission modes, or session = follow the profile's. Defaults to auto (when the harness has it). Cannot be a mode that skips all confirmations
api.field.residents.profileId: Profile id (listed by `daisy workspace catalog`): must be for this harness and on the device where the workspace lives
api.field.residents.role: Prompt layer two, "role": who it is and what service it offers to others
api.field.residents.tools: Built-in harness tools it may use (repeatable, e.g. Read, Grep, Glob); * means the harness's full default set. Only harnesses that declare support can set this (Claude Code)
api.field.sessions.pageSize: Items per page, default 20; the server clamps it to 1–100
api.field.settings.device: The device the change was made on
api.field.settings.hint: What the owner still needs to do (e.g. the command to turn on linger)
api.field.settings.linger: systemd: start at boot without logging in (loginctl linger); null if it cannot be determined
api.field.settings.manager: What starts Daisy: a systemd user unit (Linux), a launchd login item (macOS), the current user's startup entry HKCU\…\Run (Windows); null when unsupported
api.field.settings.matrix: Cells to change: kind → device → on/off
api.field.settings.reason: Why it is unsupported, e.g. "launchctl not found on this Mac"
api.field.settings.revision: The revision last read; answers 409 if it does not match
api.field.settings.supported: Whether autostart works on this system (Linux: systemd user instance; macOS: launchd login item; Windows: the current user's startup entry, which needs Daisy's Windows helper)
api.field.settings.unit: systemd unit name (daisy.service, or daisy-<hash>.service for an explicit data directory); on macOS the launchd label (ai.daisy.daisy, or ai.daisy.daisy-<hash>); on Windows the startup entry's name (Daisy, or Daisy-<hash>)
api.field.tokens.for: For whom: the contact's identity number (or a unique prefix of 8+ characters); me = myself (still only a visitor, only through the A2A entry, not given owner identity)
api.field.tokens.note: Note (who it is for, what it does, e.g. "for CI")
api.field.tokens.ttl: Validity: 7d, 12h, 30m or seconds; default 7 days, at most 90 days
api.letIn.agent-audience: change who may call it and the named-people list
api.letIn.agent-exposure: make a session public; set whether doing is allowed; create or change a resident agent
api.letIn.contact: add or remove a mutually recognised card
api.letIn.device: pair a new device, revoke a device
api.letIn.face: turn on the outside face, the outside face's one-time passcodes, the local web page's passcode
api.letIn.invoke-request: approve or deny someone else's call request
api.letIn.visitor-token: issue or revoke tokens for third-party A2A clients ({command} token, see scopes.md)
api.pin.rule.control: A PIN cannot contain control characters such as line breaks or tabs
api.pin.rule.length: A PIN has {min} to {max} characters (digits only is fine; longer is safer)
api.pin.rule.message: {problem}. Choose another one and set it again.
api.revocation.ai-tokens: the tokens fetched for the AI and the cross-Daisy access tokens issued as the AI
api.revocation.external-face: the outside face: turned off, its web sessions and unused one-time passcodes voided
api.revocation.invoke-grants: outside call grants: permanent grants, the allowlist, named-people lists, calls waiting for approval
api.revocation.issuer: the external issuer's trust and the owner tokens kept
api.revocation.visitor-tokens: the time-limited tokens issued to third-party A2A clients ({command} token)
api.route.a2a.card.description: A2A 1.0 Agent Card: two transports (JSON-RPC first), Bearer authentication, two optional extensions (act, trace), streaming and push notifications declared unsupported. Given only to people who are mutually recognised and within the audience; everyone else gets 404. `A2A-Version` is not checked.
api.route.a2a.directory.description: Lists only the agents open to this caller (mutually recognised and within the audience), each with its card address. Used by Daisy's own "discover agents" tool; a third-party client that has an agent's address can use it without this.
api.route.a2a.directory.summary: List the agents the caller can see (Daisy's agent directory, not part of A2A)
api.route.a2a.extendedCard.description: The ordinary card is already shown only to authenticated people, so an extended card would have nothing more to hold (section 5 of a2a-usage.md). Answers `ExtendedAgentCardNotConfiguredError`.
api.route.a2a.getTask.description: Only tasks you started can be queried; other people's tasks answer `TaskNotFoundError`, the same as nonexistent ones. Query parameter `historyLength`.
api.route.a2a.jsonrpc.description: Method names use the 1.0 spelling. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0`. Streaming, subscriptions, push notifications and the extended card answer the spec's unsupported errors. For error codes, see section 9 of a2a-usage.md.
api.route.a2a.listTasks.summary: List tasks (ListTasks): only those this caller started on this agent
api.route.a2a.pushConfigCreate.descripti: Not supported: push notifications. The card declares `streaming: false` / `pushNotifications: false` / `extendedAgentCard: false` (a2a-usage.md §5). Answers `PushNotificationNotSupportedError`.
api.route.a2a.pushConfigCreate.summary: Create a push notification config (not supported)
api.route.a2a.pushConfigDelete.descripti: Not supported: push notifications. The card declares `streaming: false` / `pushNotifications: false` / `extendedAgentCard: false` (a2a-usage.md §5). Answers `PushNotificationNotSupportedError`.
api.route.a2a.pushConfigDelete.summary: Delete a push notification config (not supported)
api.route.a2a.pushConfigGet.description: Not supported: push notifications. The card declares `streaming: false` / `pushNotifications: false` / `extendedAgentCard: false` (a2a-usage.md §5). Answers `PushNotificationNotSupportedError`.
api.route.a2a.pushConfigGet.summary: Read a push notification config (not supported)
api.route.a2a.pushConfigList.description: Not supported: push notifications. The card declares `streaming: false` / `pushNotifications: false` / `extendedAgentCard: false` (a2a-usage.md §5). Answers `PushNotificationNotSupportedError`.
api.route.a2a.send.description: Request body `{ message, configuration?, metadata? }`. Without `returnImmediately: true`, it waits until the task ends, needs input or needs authentication before answering (no time limit); with it, the task is returned immediately. For the rules on the three ids, see section 7 of a2a-usage.md.
api.route.a2a.stream.description: Not supported: streaming messages. The card declares `streaming: false` / `pushNotifications: false` / `extendedAgentCard: false` (a2a-usage.md §5). Answers `UnsupportedOperationError`.
api.route.a2a.stream.summary: Send a message with streaming (not supported)
api.route.a2a.taskAction.description: `:op` is `<taskId>:cancel` or `<taskId>:subscribe` (the spec's form). Only your own tasks that have not ended can be cancelled: a queued one is withdrawn, a running one is stopped, one waiting for the owner's approval stops waiting (the card stays for the owner), one needing input is cancelled outright. An ended task answers `TaskNotCancelableError`.
api.route.a2a.taskAction.summary: Cancel a task (`<taskId>:cancel`, CancelTask); subscribe to a task (`<taskId>:subscribe`, not supported)
api.route.approval.comment.description: A comment makes no decision. `requestId` is an idempotency key: a resend records only one comment.
api.route.approval.comment.summary: Comment on an approval card or ask for changes
api.route.approval.comments.summary: Read the discussion on an approval card
api.route.approval.list.description: Newest first; `before` takes those before a given time, for paging.
api.route.approval.list.field.before: Only list those earlier than this time (milliseconds)
api.route.approval.list.summary: List approval cards (by default only pending ones)
api.route.approval.respond.description: Sending the same decision again answers the original result; one already handled or no longer valid answers 409. Answers only your own AI's cards (`perm:` tool permission, `ask:` question, `block:` blocked operation). Other people's call requests (call cards, `call:…`) are listed in the approval list but are not answered here: approving or rejecting needs the PIN, through the `POST /api/requests/:rid/decision` given in the card's `respondVia` (`daisy:grant` + PIN); here a call card answers 403 `request_needs_pin`.
api.route.approval.respond.exempt: Your own AI's tool permissions and questions are answered only on the web page and paired devices (saying yes on the AI's behalf needs the owner present in person: a command-line credential may be the owner's AI)
api.route.approval.respond.summary: Answer an approval card (tool permission, a question from the AI)
api.route.attachment.download.descriptio: Common image types are returned inline; everything else as a download.
api.route.attachment.upload.description: Content goes in `data` as base64; at most 8 MiB after decoding.
api.route.attachment.upload.field.name: File name
api.route.events.list.description:
Each event is a CloudEvents 1.0 event (docs/contracts/events.md): an AI asking for approval, an AI asking a question, someone's call waiting for approval — each with an "opened" and a "resolved" kind. Ordered by `seq`, ascending; `cursor` is the last event's `seq` on this page (equal to `after` when the page is empty), to pass as `after` next time; when `hasMore` is true, read on at once.

With no new event within `wait` seconds (at most {eventsWaitMaxS}) the answer is an empty page; a new event is answered at once.

Resuming after a disconnect: a subscriber saves `cursor` after it has handled a page and reads on from it after a restart; it may read the same batch again — deduplicate by `id`. An `after` older than the events still kept (already cleaned up), or larger than the highest sequence number this Daisy has written (its data was rebuilt), answers 410 with `code: cursor_reset`: take a snapshot first, then read on from the snapshot's `cursor`.

With nobody subscribed nothing happens: events are written all the same and cleaned up after {eventsRetentionDays} days; an "opened" event of a card not yet resolved is kept until it is resolved.
api.route.events.list.summary: Read the event outlet incrementally by sequence number (long polling supported)
api.route.events.snapshot.description: Answers the "appeared" event of every card not yet settled (in ascending `seq`), plus `cursor`: use it afterwards as `after` for `GET /api/events` and no event after the snapshot will be missed. Use it on first subscribing or on receiving `cursor_reset`.
api.route.events.snapshot.summary: Snapshot of the event outlet: all cards not yet settled, and the sequence number to continue from
api.route.grant.actSet.description: A kind of "letting someone in" (kind agent-exposure): needs the PIN, and the AI cannot do it. Allowing act means letting others work on the main line under this permission mode; once it is turned off, acts still queued and not yet started are withdrawn (rejected with ACT_DISABLED), and those running finish as usual. The permission mode cannot be one that skips all confirmations. A public agent without a read-only mode (unable to accept ask) cannot turn act off (409 `act_required`: make it private first).
api.route.grant.actSet.summary: Set whether an agent allows "act" and which permission mode act uses
api.route.grant.actShow.description: Ask's read-only strength and where it runs come from this AI's capability declaration: strong / weak (relying only on the harness's plan mode) / none (cannot ask, act only); branch (read-only side branch) / main-queue (no side questions or forking, so it falls back to queueing on the main line, still read-only). Read-only: owner entries such as the web page need no PIN; the local command line does.
api.route.grant.actShow.field.aid: The agent's id (for a public agent, its session id)
api.route.grant.actShow.summary: Show how an agent accepts "ask" and "act": whether act is allowed, act's permission mode, ask's read-only strength
api.route.grant.agentList.description: Three kinds of agent: private agents are all other sessions and are not listed here; a public agent is a session set to public (`daisy agent public set`); a resident agent is a configuration (`daisy agent resident …`). Each comes with its audience, whether act is allowed, and its number of cards waiting for approval and of always-allow grants. Read-only: the web page, paired devices and tokens an external issuer gave the owner need no PIN, the local command line does (a command-line credential may be the owner's AI); `daisy:grant` is still required, so the AI and visitors cannot read it.
api.route.grant.agentList.summary: List the agents others can call (public agents and resident agents) and each one's audience
api.route.grant.audienceSet.description: One of two: open to everyone mutually recognised, or open only to named people. Needs the PIN. Narrowing takes effect immediately: calls in progress from people no longer in the audience are stopped, and waiting cards are voided. Whether it can be called at all (public, resident, private) is not changed here.
api.route.grant.audienceSet.summary: Change an agent's audience and named-people list
api.route.grant.audienceShow.description: Read-only: owner entries such as the web page need no PIN; the local command line does.
api.route.grant.audienceShow.field.aid: The agent's id (for a public agent, its session id)
api.route.grant.audienceShow.summary: Show an agent's audience (everyone mutually recognised, or only named people)
api.route.grant.contactExport.descriptio: The card holds a display name, this Daisy's public key and identity number, and addresses where it can be reached, signed by the identity key. Send the text to the other person (or save it as a .daisycard file); once they import it, they recognise you (mutual recognition needs each side to import once). The card itself carries no permissions. Read-only: owner entries such as the web page need no PIN; the local command line does.
api.route.grant.contactExport.summary: Export your identity card (a piece of text you can copy)
api.route.grant.contactImport.descriptio: A kind of "letting someone in": needs the PIN, and the AI cannot do it. The card is verified first (signature, identity number, human-readable lines); you cannot add yourself; a person already in contacts is replaced only with update, and an older card cannot replace a newer one. Only once added are the tokens they sign recognised; mutual recognition by itself carries no call permission, and only ticking the allowlist pre-approves them.
api.route.grant.contactImport.summary: Import someone's identity card (add it to contacts), optionally adding them to the allowlist too
api.route.grant.contactInspect.descripti: Reads only the text you give it; does not read or change contacts. Before importing, use it to show the owner the name and the full identity number, and ask them to check the number with the other person (over another trusted channel). Read-only: owner entries such as the web page need no PIN; the local command line does; it still needs `daisy:grant`, and the AI cannot call it.
api.route.grant.contactInspect.notLetIn: Read-only: only parses the card text given to it, verifies the signature and computes the identity number; does not read or change contacts
api.route.grant.contactInspect.summary: See whose card this is (verify the signature, compute the identity number) without adding it to contacts
api.route.grant.contactList.description: Read-only: the web page, paired devices and tokens the external issuer gave the owner need no PIN; the local command line does (a command-line credential may be the owner's AI); it still needs `daisy:grant`, so the AI and visitors cannot read it.
api.route.grant.contactList.summary: List the people in contacts (mutually recognised cards) and who is on the allowlist
api.route.grant.contactRemove.descriptio: Takes effect immediately: tokens they sign get 401 from the next request on, they are taken off the allowlist, and their calls in progress are stopped by call grants. To recognise them again, import their card again.
api.route.grant.contactRemove.summary: Remove a contact: stop recognising them
api.route.grant.contactShow.description: Read-only: owner entries such as the web page need no PIN; the local command line does.
api.route.grant.contactShow.summary: Show one contact, along with their card's text
api.route.grant.contactWhitelistAdd.desc: Pre-approves them to call all your agents that are "open to everyone mutually recognised": their first call no longer pops up a card. Only for mutually recognised people: import their card first.
api.route.grant.contactWhitelistAdd.summ: Add a contact to the allowlist
api.route.grant.contactWhitelistRemove.d: After this, when they call an agent that is "open to everyone mutually recognised", calls without a grant of their own need the owner's approval.
api.route.grant.contactWhitelistRemove.s: Remove a contact from the allowlist
api.route.grant.grantList.description: The allowlist is not here (it is a mark on contacts; see `GET /api/contacts`). Read-only: owner entries such as the web page need no PIN; the local command line does.
api.route.grant.grantList.summary: List always-allow call grants (one per agent per person)
api.route.grant.grantRevoke.description: Takes effect immediately: this person's calls in progress that came in through this grant are stopped, and calling this agent again needs approval anew. Needs the PIN.
api.route.grant.publicSet.description: A kind of "letting someone in" (kind agent-exposure): needs the PIN, and the AI cannot do it. **A public agent mixes conversations**: when visitors ask it, they can read the main line's context, and answers may reveal the owner's own work; requests marked "act" go into the main line, and the question and answer stay in the main line. For an outward service where conversations stay apart, use a resident agent. Once it is public, who can call it is decided by the audience (by default open to everyone mutually recognised, with a card on the first call; `PUT /api/agents/:aid/audience`). Refusals (409): the session is archived (`session_archived`); it is an "ask-only" side branch or a resident agent's session (`not_publishable`); the session's identity skips all confirmations (`bypass_not_private`); this AI has no read-only mode and cannot accept "ask", while "act" is off (`act_required`: such an agent can be public only when act is allowed). Making it private again takes effect immediately: outside tasks in progress or queued are stopped (rejected), cards waiting for approval are voided, and its grants, audience and ask/act settings are cleared as well; side effects already produced are not rolled back. If it is already in that state, nothing changes.
api.route.grant.publicSet.field.id: The session's id (a public agent's id is the same)
api.route.grant.publicSet.summary: Make a session a public agent, or make it private again
api.route.grant.requestDecide.descriptio: A kind of "letting someone in": needs the PIN, and the AI cannot do it. Sending the same decision again answers the original result; one already handled with a different decision, expired or voided answers 409. If things have changed by the time of approval (the other person was removed from contacts, the agent was made private again or is no longer open to them), the card is voided and it answers 409 `request_stale`.
api.route.grant.requestDecide.field.rid: The request's id (`call:…`; `call:` can be omitted)
api.route.grant.requestDecide.summary: Approve or reject a call request: always allow, allow once, reject
api.route.grant.requestList.description: By default lists only those waiting for approval. The same card also appears in the approval list (`GET /api/approvals`, `kind: "call"`), but can be approved or rejected only here (needs the PIN). Reading: owner entries such as the web page need no PIN; the local command line does; it still needs `daisy:grant`: the AI and visitors cannot read it.
api.route.grant.requestList.field.status: Waiting for approval, handled or all
api.route.grant.requestList.summary: List other people's requests to call my agents (cards waiting for approval)
api.route.grant.requestShow.description: Read-only: owner entries such as the web page need no PIN; the local command line does.
api.route.grant.requestShow.field.rid: The request's id (`call:…`; `call:` can be omitted)
api.route.grant.residentClose.descriptio: No PIN needed: closing only takes back and lets nobody in. Its grants, audience and cards waiting for approval are deleted with it, calls in progress stop (refused), and its card and address go away; the dedicated sessions are archived and their processes stopped, with records kept and readable. A closed agent cannot be resumed; to offer the service again, create a new one.
api.route.grant.residentClose.notLetIn: Closing only takes back calls and grants and lets nobody in (narrowing needs no PIN)
api.route.grant.residentClose.summary: Close a resident agent: it stops accepting calls, tasks in progress stop, dedicated sessions close (records are kept)
api.route.grant.residentCreate.descripti: A kind of "let someone in" (kind agent-exposure): needs the PIN, and the AI cannot do it. Once created, it can be called by mutually recognised people (the audience defaults to everyone mutually recognised, and the first call raises a card; narrow it with `daisy agent audience set`). Each visiting conversation starts its own dedicated session, and they cannot see one another. The profile cannot be in a mode that skips all confirmations.
api.route.grant.residentDelete.descripti: No PIN needed: deleting only takes back and lets nobody in. It first takes everything back as "close" does, then deletes the configuration and the dedicated sessions' records.
api.route.grant.residentDelete.notLetIn: Deleting only takes back calls, grants and sessions and lets nobody in (narrowing needs no PIN)
api.route.grant.residentDelete.summary: Delete a resident agent and all its dedicated sessions
api.route.grant.residentList.description: Read-only: the web page, paired devices and tokens an external issuer gave the owner need no PIN, the local command line does (a command-line credential may be the owner's AI); `daisy:grant` is still required, so the AI and visitors cannot read it.
api.route.grant.residentPause.descriptio: No PIN needed: pausing only takes back and lets nobody in. Tasks still queued and not started are refused as well (AGENT_PAUSED); a turn already running finishes as usual.
api.route.grant.residentPause.notLetIn: Pausing only stops accepting calls and lets nobody in (narrowing needs no PIN)
api.route.grant.residentPause.summary: Pause a resident agent: later calls are refused (AGENT_PAUSED)
api.route.grant.residentResume.descripti: Needs the PIN: resuming lets others call it again.
api.route.grant.residentSet.description: Needs the PIN (tightening counts as a change too). The harness, workspace and profile cannot be changed after creation. New settings take effect from the next turn; if directories or tools changed, the dedicated sessions' processes restart on the next turn.
api.route.grant.residentSet.summary: Change a resident agent: name, prompt, permission mode, directories, tools, concurrency, usage, how confirmations are handled
api.route.grant.residentShow.description: Read-only: owner entry points such as the web page need no PIN, the local command line does.
api.route.grant.residentShow.summary: Show a resident agent: configuration, layered prompts, usage, visiting conversations
api.route.grant.tokenIssue.description: A kind of "let someone in" (kind visitor-token): needs the PIN, and the AI cannot do it. The issued token: `iss` and `aud` are this Daisy; `sub` is that contact (yourself for `me`); `scope` is only `daisy:invoke`; `client_id` is `token:<jti>`; there is no `act`. Whoever holds it calls through A2A as that contact and still has to pass call grants (audience, allowlist, cards); one issued for `me` also only goes through the A2A entry and cannot reach the local API. The token appears only in this one answer; Daisy stores only the issue record (jti, for whom, note, expiry), not the token itself: whoever gets it can call as that identity, so keep it like a password. It is voided when the contact is removed or the PIN is reset.
api.route.grant.tokenIssue.summary: Issue a time-limited token to a third-party A2A client (daisy token)
api.route.grant.tokenList.description: By default lists only those still valid; `state=all` also lists expired and revoked ones (kept 30 days). Read-only: the web page, paired devices and tokens an external issuer gave the owner need no PIN, the local command line does (a command-line credential may be the owner's AI); `daisy:grant` is still required, so the AI and visitors cannot read it.
api.route.grant.tokenList.field.state: active: still valid; all: also expired and revoked ones (kept 30 days)
api.route.grant.tokenList.summary: List tokens issued to third-party A2A clients (records only, not the tokens themselves)
api.route.grant.tokenRevoke.description: Takes effect immediately: requests carrying it are refused (401) from the next one on. Tasks already started are not affected (to stop them, withdraw the grant or take the agent back). Needs the PIN. Revoking an already revoked token again answers with the original record.
api.route.grant.tokenRevoke.field.jti: Token id (the jti in `daisy token list`)
api.route.grant.tokenRevoke.summary: Revoke a token issued to a third-party A2A client
api.route.profile.autoCompact.summary: Show a profile's auto-compact threshold and whether each live process is already using it
api.route.profile.autoCompactRestart.des: Interrupts whatever those processes are doing; check `interrupts` with `show` first.
api.route.profile.autoCompactRestart.sum: Restart now the live processes not yet using the new threshold
api.route.profile.create.description: API key profiles are only for Claude and compatible services; other agents sign in with `login`.
api.route.profile.create.summary: Create a profile (API key, or reuse a CLI already signed in on this machine)
api.route.profile.createManaged.descript: Once created, sign in with `daisy login start <id>`; the machine's existing CLI credentials are left untouched.
api.route.profile.createManaged.summary: Create a separately signed-in profile (subscription sign-in, with its own CLI directory)
api.route.profile.delete.description: Refused while tasks are still queued or running; unfinished sign-ins are cancelled with it. Sessions that used it stay readable but can no longer send messages.
api.route.profile.login.summary: Show a sign-in flow's state and authorization URL
api.route.profile.loginInput.summary: Submit the authorization code from the authorization page
api.route.profile.loginStart.description: If a sign-in is already in progress, answers with that one. Then use `login show` to see the authorization URL, and `login input` to submit the authorization code when needed.
api.route.profile.loginStart.summary: Start signing in to a harness (separately signed-in profile)
api.route.profile.update.description: With `model`, this is the whole set of model settings (fields left out are cleared); with only `autoCompactTokens`, only the threshold changes and the answer includes `autoCompact`.
api.route.profile.update.summary: Change a profile's model, reasoning effort, permission mode, model slots and auto-compact threshold
api.route.session.activity.description: `items` is empty when the session is not live.
api.route.session.activity.summary: What the live process has been doing recently
api.route.session.aiToken.description: Callable only with the current turn's AI work credential (`DAISY_AI_CREDENTIAL_FILE`), so it is available only while a turn is in progress. The token names the owner (sub) and the AI actually acting (act), its scope never exceeds the owner's, and it is valid for at most 1 hour; for the same session, audience and scope, the same token is given back while more than 5 minutes remain (even across turns), otherwise a new one is obtained; each session keeps at most 16 tokens and may obtain at most 10 new ones per minute (beyond that it answers 429). In external mode it performs an RFC 8693 token exchange with the external issuer; in standalone mode this Daisy signs it itself.
api.route.session.aiToken.exempt: For the AI's own use: an MCP in the harness calls it with the current turn's AI work credential; the owner and the command line do not need to get tokens on the AI's behalf
api.route.session.aiToken.notLetIn: Gets a token for this turn's AI to access other systems (daisy:tools, without daisy:grant, ≤ 1 hour); lets nobody into this Daisy
api.route.session.aiToken.summary: Get a token on behalf of this AI (for an MCP in the harness that needs one)
api.route.session.answerApproval.descrip: Permission confirmations must be answered on the "Approvals" page (`approval.respond`); here they answer 409 `approval_elsewhere`.
api.route.session.answerApproval.exempt: Your own AI's tool permissions and questions are answered only on the web page and paired devices (saying yes on the AI's behalf needs the owner present in person: a command-line credential may be the owner's AI)
api.route.session.answerApproval.field.a: Answers to each of the questions asked
api.route.session.answerApproval.summary: Answer the AI's question in the conversation
api.route.session.backgroundStop.descrip: Ids starting with `scheduler:` are Daisy schedules or background commands and are cancelled immediately (the old `harbor:` prefix is also accepted); the rest are the agent's background tasks, handed to the live process to stop. Only the session's owner can stop them.
api.route.session.backgroundStop.summary: Stop an item under "Background" (an agent's background task or a Daisy schedule)
api.route.session.cancel.description: Queued messages are kept. Side effects already produced are not rolled back.
api.route.session.create.description: `requestId` is an idempotency key: sending the same key again answers the original session (with `duplicate: true`). New sessions are always private; making a session public is a separate `daisy:grant` endpoint that needs the PIN (`daisy agent public set`).
api.route.session.delete.description: Stops all its work and hides it immediately; if no turn is running, its data is cleared immediately. `stopping: true` means a turn is still being ended; the data is cleared once it ends.
api.route.session.events.description: At most 500 per call; when `hasMore` is true, continue reading from the last one's sequence number.
api.route.session.events.field.after: Read after this sequence number, default 0
api.route.session.events.summary: Read session events incrementally by sequence number
api.route.session.freshIdentity.descript: Use it when switching identity could not carry the conversation history over and the old identity is no longer in use. From the next message on, a new native session is started (the conversation view keeps all items).
api.route.session.freshIdentity.summary: Continue without history: give up the native history that cannot be carried over
api.route.session.harnessConfig.descript: Runs asynchronously like a native operation, with the result queried via `session.operationStatus`, but what it changes is the harness configuration under this profile (every future session is affected), so it counts as "manage" (`daisy:manage`), not a session operation.
api.route.session.harnessConfig.summary: Change the configuration of the harness the session uses: config files, MCP servers, plugins, skills
api.route.session.items.field.limit: Number of items, default 200 (conversation view: default 20, at most 100)
api.route.session.items.field.view: Conversation view of a resident session; ignored for other sessions
api.route.session.items.summary: Page backwards: the items before a given one
api.route.session.list.description: Sorted by most recently updated; deleted sessions and "ask-only" side sessions are not listed.
api.route.session.list.field.taskId: Only list sessions related to this task
api.route.session.notifications.descript: Each notification is answered only as it is now (its latest revision): a pending approval is `pending`; once the approval is handled or withdrawn it is `handled` / `canceled` / `expired`; everything else is `unread` (each UI tracks read state itself). Ordered by last change, newest first.
api.route.session.notifications.summary: List the session's notifications: turn finished, approval cards, AI errors
api.route.session.offline.description: The process closes at the runner's next report; `stopping` means there really is a process to close.
api.route.session.offline.summary: Take a session offline: close its live process
api.route.session.operation.description: Asynchronous: answers the operation's id; query the result with `session.operationStatus`. The result of `fork` is in the new session (the answer's `sessionId`). Refused while the session has queued or running work. `args.count` for `rewind` is how many turns to rewind (1–10000, default 1). `fork`, `compact` and `rewind` (with `files: true`, it also needs "undo files when rewinding") require the session's AI to declare that capability (the snapshot's `features`); otherwise it answers 409 `capability_unsupported`, and `fix` says what to do.
api.route.session.operation.field.name: Operation name (the ones that change harness settings go through `session operation harness`; opening a terminal goes through `session terminal open`)
api.route.session.operation.summary: Run a native operation on a session (list models, fork, rewind, compact, etc.)
api.route.session.operationStatus.summar: Check a native operation's status and result
api.route.session.outgoingList.descripti: One entry each time the AI's `call_agent` tool sends: whose agent it called and which one, ask or act, how far the other side has got, the answer, and the chain id. Newest first. Read-only; answers are cut to 2000 characters here (use `GET /api/calls/:cid` for the full text).
api.route.session.outgoingList.field.con: Only calls to this contact (identity number)
api.route.session.outgoingList.field.ses: Only calls sent from this session (which of my AIs)
api.route.session.outgoingList.field.sta: open: not finished yet (including those waiting for my AI to add more); settled: finished; all: everything
api.route.session.outgoingList.summary: List the calls my AI made to other people's agents (whom my AI called)
api.route.session.outgoingShow.field.cid: Id of the call (`daisy call list`)
api.route.session.outgoingShow.summary: Show one call by my AI: what it sent, the other side's state, the full answer
api.route.session.promptApply.summary: Compact now and put the new prompt into effect
api.route.session.promptExtra.descriptio: Resident agents and "ask-only" side branches cannot be changed here.
api.route.session.promptExtra.summary: Change the session's own prompt supplement
api.route.session.promptShow.summary: Show a session's layered prompts and whether they are in effect
api.route.session.publicShow.description: Reads your own session, no PIN needed (making it public or private again is a `PUT` on the same address and needs the PIN). `blocked` says why it cannot be made public now; `crossTalk` is what the owner should be told before making it public (a public agent mixes conversations).
api.route.session.publicShow.summary: See whether a session is a public agent and whether it can be made public now
api.route.session.queue.summary: List queued messages (steered-but-unread first, then queue-jumped ones)
api.route.session.queueJump.description: The running turn is not interrupted; the message goes to the front and is sent as the next turn.
api.route.session.queueJump.summary: Jump the queue: start a queued message immediately
api.route.session.queueMergeJump.descrip: Messages from different sources cannot be combined into one; each becomes its own message, queued one after another behind it.
api.route.session.queueMergeJump.summary: Merge and jump: combine the selected queued messages into one and jump the queue
api.route.session.queueMergeSteer.descri: Answers 409 when no turn is running or some message cannot be steered in; answers 409 `capability_unsupported` when the session's AI has not declared "steer while running".
api.route.session.queueMergeSteer.summar: Merge and steer: combine the selected queued messages into one and send it into the running turn
api.route.session.queueRemove.summary: Remove a queued message (withdraw it if steered in but not yet read)
api.route.session.queueRemoveMany.descri: Each works the same as removing it individually; `all` skips those the AI has already read. Answers a result for each message.
Ids of the selected queued messages
api.route.session.queueRemoveMany.summar: Remove queued messages in bulk (selected ones, or all)
api.route.session.queueResume.summary: Resume a paused queue: send the next queued message
api.route.session.recoveries.summary: List recovery records left by interrupted turns (latest 50)
api.route.session.recoveryEvents.summary: Read a recovery record's events, page by page
api.route.session.scheduleAdd.descriptio: Only `kind` is checked here; the other fields are checked again by the scheduler as a ScheduleCreate (`delaySeconds`, `cron`, `prompt`, `label`…). Only the session's owner can set one.
api.route.session.scheduleAdd.summary: Set a timer (one-time wake-up or recurring cron)
api.route.session.scheduleCancel.summary: Cancel a timer or background command
api.route.session.scheduleList.descripti: Includes the turns used today and the server time zone (cron is interpreted in it).
api.route.session.scheduleList.summary: List a session's timers and background commands
api.route.session.scheduleUpdate.descrip: The cron, prompt, label and end time can be changed; a one-time timer can have its fire time changed. Background commands cannot be changed.
api.route.session.scheduleUpdate.summary: Change a timer that is still waiting
api.route.session.send.description: With `delivery: "queue"` it goes into the queue; while a turn is running it is also queued after that turn. `requestId` is an idempotency key: sending the same key again answers the original message (with `duplicate: true`). Refused while the resident agent is paused.
api.route.session.send.summary: Send a message to a session
api.route.session.shellRun.description: Only in your own sessions; the command is queued for the runner, and you get the result with `session shell status`.
api.route.session.shellRun.summary: Run a command in the session's working directory
api.route.session.shellStatus.summary: Read a command's status and output
api.route.session.show.description: Without parameters, answers a full snapshot; `tail` takes only the latest few items; `since` (plus `from`) takes only the changes after the client's version, falling back to a snapshot when that is not possible.
api.route.session.show.field.from: id of the earliest item held by the client (used with since)
api.route.session.show.field.since: Cursor held by the client: answer only the changes after it
api.route.session.show.field.tail: Take only the latest N items (0 = all)
api.route.session.show.field.view: Conversation view of a resident session; ignored for other sessions
api.route.session.show.summary: Read a session: settings, items and cursor
api.route.session.steer.description: When the running turn is not the owner's own (someone else's request, the AI's own, a wake-up), the message is queued after it instead (`queued: true` plus `reason`). Answers 409 `capability_unsupported` when the session's AI has not declared "steer while running" (snapshot `features.steer` is `none`, e.g. Kimi Code). `requestId` is an idempotency key.
api.route.session.steer.summary: Steer now: send a message into the running turn
api.route.session.switchIdentity.descrip: Only for the session's owner, only for Claude Code sessions, and only with no turn queued or running. A model chosen for this session alone is cleared, and the new identity's model is used.
api.route.session.switchIdentity.summary: Switch identity: the session continues with another of your profiles
api.route.session.terminalInput.auditWhy: Keystroke-level input and window sizes would flood the audit if recorded one by one; the message that opened the terminal is already recorded
api.route.session.terminalInput.descript: The request body's `id` is this input's dedup key: the same id is accepted only once (the command line generates it automatically).
api.route.session.terminalInput.summary: Type text into the terminal or resize its window
api.route.session.terminalList.summary: The session's most recent terminal task
api.route.session.terminalOpen.descripti: Runs asynchronously like a native operation; query its status with `session.operationStatus`, and read and write with `session terminal output` / `input`. Off by default on the outside face (the terminal switch).
api.route.session.terminalOpen.summary: Open a terminal in the session's working directory
api.route.session.terminalOutput.descrip: At most 100 chunks each time; `truncated` means earlier output is no longer kept.
api.route.session.terminalOutput.field.a: Read after this sequence number; default 0
api.route.session.terminalOutput.summary: Read terminal output incrementally by sequence number
api.route.session.update.description: Archiving stops everything the session is doing and cancels its schedules. Setting a model or reasoning effort for a single session requires the session's AI to declare "switch model" / "switch reasoning effort"; otherwise it answers 409 `capability_unsupported`.
api.route.session.update.field.relatedTa: Related task ids to keep; those not listed are removed, none are added
api.route.session.update.field.settings: This session's model, reasoning effort, etc.; an empty string means use the profile's
api.route.session.update.summary: Change a session: title, archiving, related tasks, model and reasoning effort
api.route.settings.autostartSet.descript: Linux: generates and enables (or disables and removes) a user-level systemd unit, no root needed; macOS: writes (or removes) a login item in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, started by launchd after the owner logs in, no administrator needed. Turning it off does not stop a running Daisy. Windows is not supported yet and answers `supported: false` with the reason.
api.route.settings.autostartSet.field.en: true to turn on, false to turn off
api.route.settings.autostartSet.notLetIn: Autostart only affects when Daisy runs on this machine; lets nobody in
api.route.settings.autostartStatus.summa: Show autostart: whether it is supported, whether it is on, what starts Daisy
api.route.settings.deviceForget.descript: Callable only by the paired device itself; voids its own device credential and all its sessions. Only narrows, no PIN needed.
api.route.settings.deviceForget.exempt: Used by the paired device's own web page; the command line has no device to unpair
api.route.settings.deviceForget.notLetIn: A device cancels its own pairing; only narrows who can connect
api.route.settings.deviceForget.summary: Unpair this device ("Sign out" on the phone)
api.route.settings.deviceList.descriptio: By default lists only the ones still valid; `state=all` also lists revoked and expired ones (kept for 30 days). `pairLocks`: sources whose pairing is paused because of wrong pairing codes (per source: for direct connections, the address seen by the listener; for relayed ones, the address the relay reports) and until when; `pairLockedUntil`: the latest of those (null if none). Read-only: the web page, paired devices and tokens the external issuer gave the owner need no PIN; the local command line does (a command-line credential may be the owner's AI); it still needs `daisy:grant`, so the AI and visitors cannot read it.
api.route.settings.deviceList.field.stat: active: only the ones still valid; all: also lists revoked and expired ones (kept for 30 days)
api.route.settings.deviceList.summary: List paired devices (records only, no credentials)
api.route.settings.deviceRevoke.descript: Takes effect immediately: its device credential and sessions are voided, its connected realtime channels are disconnected at once (close code 4401: device revoked), and requests being processed answer 401. Needs the PIN (pairing and revoking devices fall under the same PIN-protected permission). Revoking an already revoked device again answers the original record.
api.route.settings.deviceRevoke.field.id: Device id (the id in daisy device list)
api.route.settings.deviceSession.descrip: A device session lasts at most {deviceSessionHours} hours (a credential coming in as the owner from elsewhere: the one sent with each request lasts no more than 24 hours); when it expires the web page trades the device credential for a new one. A revoked device, one unused for {deviceIdleDays} days, or one not on the face it was paired on → 401 device_invalid. At most {deviceSessionPerMinute} calls per address per minute.
api.route.settings.deviceSession.exempt: Used by a paired device's web page to get its own session credential; the command line uses the local credential
api.route.settings.deviceSession.notLetI: A paired device gets a new session credential: the device itself was let in by pairing, which needs the PIN, and once revoked it immediately can no longer get one
api.route.settings.deviceSession.summary: A paired device exchanges its device credential for a new device session
api.route.settings.externalOff.descripti: Narrows who can connect, so no PIN needed. Web sessions on the outside face are voided along with it.
api.route.settings.externalOff.notLetIn: Turns off the outside face; only narrows who can connect
api.route.settings.externalOn.descriptio: Widens who can connect, so it needs the PIN. Turning it on enables the passcode automatically. Plain HTTP is allowed only on loopback, overlay network or private network addresses (127/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, ::1, fc00::/7). TLS uses the self-signed certificate in keys/: a new one is generated only when there is none yet, when it does not cover the listen address, or when it expires within a day (written to the log and the audit); when the certificate files exist but cannot be used (wrong owner, key and certificate not a pair, unreadable), it answers 409 `tls_refused` and does not quietly replace the certificate.
api.route.settings.externalOn.summary: Turn on or change the outside face (listen address, port, TLS, switches such as the terminal)
api.route.settings.issuerRefresh.descrip: Normally fetched automatically according to the cache headers (every hour if there are none), and also on an unknown kid; use this after the issuer rotates its keys if you want that to take effect immediately.
api.route.settings.issuerRefresh.notLetI: Refetches the configured issuer's key set; does not change whom it trusts
api.route.settings.issuerRefresh.summary: Fetch the external issuer's key set again now
api.route.settings.issuerRemove.descript: Narrows who can connect, no PIN needed (like turning off the outside face). The cached public keys and the owner's token are deleted too, and tokens obtained for the AI are no longer renewed.
api.route.settings.issuerRemove.notLetIn: Stops trusting the external issuer; only narrows who can connect
api.route.settings.issuerRemove.summary: Stop trusting the external issuer and go back to self-issuing
api.route.settings.issuerSet.description: A kind of "letting someone in": from then on, tokens the issuer signs for the owner get the owner's identity (no pairing needed), and tokens signed for anyone else can only use the A2A entry. Needs the PIN, and the AI cannot do it. When configuring, the metadata and key set are fetched once, and nothing is saved if they cannot be fetched; after that, verification is offline, with key rotation by kid.
api.route.settings.issuerSet.summary: Configure an external issuer (trust the tokens it signs)
api.route.settings.issuerShow.descriptio: The answer includes this Daisy's public key (JWK): register it with the external issuer so the issuer can verify the client assertion (private_key_jwt) when Daisy exchanges tokens for the AI. Contains no tokens.
api.route.settings.issuerShow.summary: Show the token issuer: self-issued or external issuer, who the owner is, the cached public keys
api.route.settings.languageSet.descripti: The web page, the command line, the local API's messages and the prompts of new sessions use it; a session already running keeps its language, new sessions use the new one. While {product} is not running, {command} language set and {command} language show read and write config.json in the data directory themselves (the setting applies at the next start).
api.route.settings.languageSet.field.lan: Language (en, zh-CN, ...; see available in language show); null follows the system
api.route.settings.languageSet.notLetIn: The display language only decides the text the owner sees; lets nobody in and does not change what this machine runs
api.route.settings.languageSet.summary: Set the display language (null: follow the system)
api.route.settings.languageShow.summary: Show the display language: the owner's setting, the one in use, the ones available
